written: 2026-11-16, committed before the runs that rate the pin's mutants (the commit that adds this file is the timestamp): the exact allocation's tie window, TIE_ULPS, whose change was invisible to the allocator tests because their oracle imported the constant
phase: allocator test pin: the oracle carries its own 64 and the two-sided rule
labels: predictions by the pinning agent (Sonnet) from two local single runs of each mutant (not rates); test-side only, no src/ change
seen_before: PR 323's review: TIE_ULPS x16 in the law went unseen, 0 of 8 runs, because tests/control/allocation_draws.py imported the law's constant for its tie window

locally, one run of each mutant over the new tests: x16 fails the direct pin and the two 1.05 cases (float64, float32), passes the 0.95 cases; /4 fails the direct pin and the two 0.95 cases, passes the 1.05 cases; the clean run passes all seven (the premise, the oracle's own gap over its own window, measured within 0.04 of the nominal ratio in both dtypes)

operating_point.platform: CPU, the laptop (JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu); each run a fresh process
operating_point.sizes_and_parameters: a constructed two-face problem, rows diag(0.001, 1) over unit scales, wanted (0.001 (1 - g), 0.3), limits +-1, reference (1, 0.3): the free face (residual zero) and the bound face (residual 0.001 g, effort zero) differ in residual by 0.95 and by 1.05 of the oracle's two-sided window; no Hypothesis draw: deterministic
operating_point.mutants: the law's TIE_ULPS patched in the test module's context to 64 x 16 = 1024 (ALLOCATION_PLANT=tie_x16) and 64 / 4 = 16 (ALLOCATION_PLANT=tie_div4)

gate_1_window_x16_is_caught.claim: a law whose tie window is 16 times wider is caught on every run, and the unplanted arm is quiet
gate_1_window_x16_is_caught.case: tests/control/test_exact_allocation.py::test_the_law_ties_two_faces_just_inside_its_window_and_not_just_outside (the 1.05 cases fail) and ::test_the_laws_tie_window_is_the_oracles_declared_64_ulps, ALLOCATION_PLANT=tie_x16; each node rated alone

prediction.basis: derived: the 1.05 pair's residual gap is 0.066 of the x16 window, so the law ties and takes the bound face; the pin compares 1024 with the literal 64. Neither depends on a draw or a seed
prediction.why: deterministic problem and a deterministic comparison

gate_1_window_x16_is_caught.if_wrong: read the missed seed's output: a miss means the faces' tie did not follow the window (the switch's argmin or the premise's margin), not a rounding draw
gate_1_window_x16_is_caught.cannot_discriminate_if: the premise's ratio leaves its band in some dtype (the test then fails clean, which the clean arm shows)

gate_2_window_div4_is_caught.claim: a law whose tie window is a quarter as wide is caught on every run, and the unplanted arm is quiet
gate_2_window_div4_is_caught.case: the same node, the 0.95 cases fail, and the direct pin, ALLOCATION_PLANT=tie_div4

prediction.basis: derived: the 0.95 pair's gap is 3.8 of the /4 window, so the law does not tie and takes the free face; the pin compares 16 with 64

bounds_and_estimates: the pin is an equality on a declared constant and a behavioural check of its two-sided rule on one constructed pair of faces at 0.95 and 1.05 of the window: it bounds nothing about the law's accuracy. A 95 % lower bound after 20 of 20 catches is 0.86

outcomes.written: 2026-11-16, after the runs; the predictions above are unchanged
outcomes.runs: local, the laptop, CPU, .github/probe/detection_rate.py, 20 fresh processes planted and 20 clean per node and plant (the clean arm is the same node with the variable removed)

gate_1_window_x16_is_caught.value: tie_x16: the two-faces node caught 20/20 and the direct pin 20/20, clean 0/20 flagged on each, none inconclusive (95 % lower bound 0.861)

gate_2_window_div4_is_caught.value: tie_div4: the two-faces node caught 20/20 and the direct pin 20/20, clean 0/20 flagged on each, none inconclusive (95 % lower bound 0.861)

outcomes.note: the two-faces node alone catches each mutant on its own side (x16 at the 1.05 cases, /4 at the 0.95 cases); the direct pin is a second, independent catch
